head: WalkAware: Apple Watch app shows nearby places and landmarks
dek: WalkAware lists museums, libraries, historic buildings and other landmarks near you right on your Apple Watch, using Apple Maps and Wikidata. It costs $2.99 with no subscription, account or ads, and was #63 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 24 November.
details: It shows up to 60 places within five kilometres and the nearest one first; distances are in a straight line, not walking routes. Where it finds a matching Wikipedia article, you can read part of it on the watch. A watch-face complication, background discovery (off by default) and an alert when you're about 200 metres from a place are optional. The developer, Mohamed Abdelsalam, says it is a discovery aid, not navigation; it came out on 22 November, needs watchOS 10 and is in English only.
where: Apple Watch (watchOS 10 or later), App Store, $2.99
means: If you like walking around a new city without staring at your phone, your watch can point out what's nearby. It's not for directions, so keep a maps app for getting there.
todo: Turn on background discovery or arrival alerts only if you want them. The developer's privacy label says it collects approximate location linked to you, so check it before you buy.
